### Tiberium Wars with Kane's Wrath (`cnc3`)

Written in batch R2 preparation, before any `cnc3` unit is coded, for Kane's Wrath patch 1.02, from the Tiberium Wars, Kane's Wrath and Ultimate Collection manuals, the wiki's transcript of the in-game Intelligence Database, a 2006 report of the interface, and EA's released Kane's Wrath XML (electronicarts/CnC_Modding_Support, folder `Kanes Wrath/Xml`, read from raw.githubusercontent.com; see the research notes).

- **The in-game role line cannot be read.** Each unit's data names a type-line string and a description string for the build tooltip and the selection panel (the `TypeDescription` and `Description` keys in EA's XML, such as `Type:GDIRiflemanSquad`), but the words live in the game's compiled string file, which EA's release leaves out, and no page read copies them. So there is no readable designation, and whether the tooltips carry strong-against or weak-against lines is unchecked.
  - The selection panel also shows a "combat chain": a green icon for the unit's weapon type and what it beats, a red one for the unit's own type and the weapons that beat it (WorthPlaying's report of EA's interface reveal, 17 October 2006: https://worthplaying.com/article/2006/10/17/news/37076-command-conquer-tiberium-wars-user-interface-details-screens/). They are pictures and no source lists them per unit, so roles step 4 cannot read them.
  - The UnitBox `role` field (Basic infantry, Deployable artillery walker) may echo that hidden type line, but no page says so: treat it as the wiki's words.
- **Official text 1: the manuals.** One paragraph per unit, then Requirements, Abilities and Upgrades lines; no strong-against or weak-against lines. Units have no readable designation, so the paragraph is the official one-line description for roles step 1.
  - Tiberium Wars manual (2007), https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/5/51/Command_and_Conquer_3_Tiberium_Wars_Manual.pdf/revision/latest. A scan with no text layer: read the page images (each PDF page is a printed spread). GDI units are on PDF pages 16 and 17 (printed 28 to 30), Nod units on 20 and 21 (printed 36 to 38), Scrin units on 24 and 25 (printed 44 to 46). The wiki's transcript, https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Command_%26_Conquer_3:_Tiberium_Wars_manual, stops after the GDI infantry. The Kane Edition reprint (https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/7/77/TW_Kane_Manual.pdf/revision/latest) has the same paragraphs behind an unusable OCR layer.
  - Kane's Wrath manual (2008), https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/1/19/CC3KWpcMANfinal.pdf/revision/latest, with a text layer. Its section New Units, Structures, and Powers (printed pages 13 to 28) covers every unit the expansion added, by faction and subfaction (the Rocket Harvester is the one KW unit not found in it). A unit it leaves out keeps its Tiberium Wars paragraph. The wiki's transcript, https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Command_%26_Conquer_3:_Kane%27s_Wrath_manual, stops after GDI.
  - Ultimate Collection manual (English, never shipped; both games in one, with a text layer): https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/8/8b/CCUC-CNC3-pcMANOLeUS.pdf/revision/latest. It reprints both sets of paragraphs and is the easiest to search, but rewrites a few (its Seeker is suited to scouting and skirmishing, with discs good against vehicles and aircraft; the 2007 manual only says it seems built for scouting) and gets some Requirements wrong (Tech Lab, a Nod building, for the Annihilator Tripod and Devastator Warship). Read the shipped manuals first; extra role or matchup words in the reprint count as official text too, with an uncertain entry naming both versions.
  - Requirements lines predate the patches. The 2007 manual puts the Beam Cannon behind the Tech Lab and the Stealth Tank behind the Operations Center; in Kane's Wrath 1.02 it is the other way round (EA's XML `GameDependency`; the infoboxes agree), and the Stealth Tank already needed the Tech Lab in Tiberium Wars 1.09. Take tiers from the infobox and the XML, never from a manual.
  - Cite a manual as kind official. The copy-check cannot read PDFs, so check paraphrases of them by hand.
- **Official text 2: the Intelligence Database**, the in-game entries unlocked in the campaigns, transcribed on https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Intelligence_Database. Cite that page as kind wiki, with a note that it copies the in-game database and the entry's name; the copy-check can read it. Its texts were written for the 2007 and 2008 releases: take role words and matchups from them, never numbers.
  - Entries exist for most Tiberium Wars GDI and Nod units (GDI tab Weapons, Tactics and Systems: Riflemen, Missile Squad, Engineer, MCV, APC, Grenadier, Sniper Team, Orca, Commando, Predator, Zone Troopers, Firehawk, Surveyor, Rig; Nod tab Kane's Arsenal: Militants and Rocket Troopers, Fanatics, Saboteur, Shadow Team, Venom, flame weapons, Vertigo, Stealth Tank, Commando, Avatar, Beam Cannon; the GDI InOps tab adds entries on Nod aircraft, the Flame Tank and Avatar, and the Scrin Tripod and Mastermind) and for most units Kane's Wrath added (Nod tab Weaponry; not the Titan, Wolverine, Mobile Repair Transport, Zone Shatterer, ZOCOM Orca, Reckoner, Mantis, Ravager or Mechapede). Other Scrin units of Tiberium Wars have none.
  - Roles step 1 reads the manual paragraph. A database entry counts as official text for step 4, for roles.secondary step 1 (a label in it) and for the drop rule.
- **Roles step 1, what the paragraphs name.** A paragraph names a role only through a label or alias that describes the unit's own job, in any word form; the unit's name counts when it names that job. Each role is still subject to its requires.
  - Name a role: scout, the Pitbull (its paragraph makes it GDI's chief scout vehicle), the Attack Bike (Nod's ultimate scout), the Orca (scouting is the first of the roles its paragraph lists) and, unless the lead reads it as a hedge, the Seeker (the 2007 paragraph says it seems built for scouting; the reprint calls it well suited to scouting); scout through recon, the Sniper Team (trained in reconnaissance); siege, the Juggernaut (walking artillery and a siege weapon), the Specter (a stealth artillery tank) and the Behemoth (long-range artillery; "support" there means firepower and names nothing); anti-armour, the Missile Squad (heavy anti-vehicle weapons; the label sits on its only weapon, so it describes the unit's job); anti-air, the Mantis (a dedicated anti-air vehicle); anti-infantry and anti-air, the Shard Walker (among the strongest of both; the bonus test picks anti-air, from its double damage to aircraft); raider, the Ravager (hit-and-run attacks); transport, the APC and the Reckoner (armoured personnel carrier, "the Reckoner APC"); support, the Mobile Repair Transport (repairs nearby vehicles); engineer, the Engineer and Combat Engineer; infiltrator, the Saboteur (its name); logistics, every harvester.
  - Name no role: the Rifleman Squad (mainstay of the ground forces), Predator (an armour-piercing cannon is a weapon, not a job), Mammoth Tank, Titan, Grenadier Squad (close-assault infantry: assault alone names nothing), Commando, Zone Trooper, Zone Raider, Scorpion Tank, Stealth Tank, Flame Tank, Avatar, Black Hand, Militant squads, Venom (a patrol craft), Stormrider (a fast-attack aircraft), Annihilator Tripod, Devourer, Gun Walker, the Awakened and Enlightened, the Confessor Cabal and Purifier (they lift nearby troops: buffer has no alias, so step 1 gives nothing).
  - A label on one of several weapons is not the unit's job and counts only for that weapon at roles.secondary step 3: the Zone Raider's anti-air rockets beside its sonic shells.
- **Strong against and weak against (roles step 4 and the roles.secondary drop rule).** No separate lines anywhere readable; read the manual paragraph and the database entry.
  - Strong, naming a kind of target: the Commando (infantry), Raider Buggy (infantry and light targets), Zone Trooper (infantry and vehicles, infantry first), Militant Rocket Squad (aircraft and armoured vehicles), Attack Bike and Slingshot (aircraft), Venom (infantry, then aircraft and some vehicles), Gun Walker (infantry and aircraft), Reaper Tripod (the toughest armour), ZOCOM Orca (vehicles and structures), Shatterer (buildings and slow vehicles), Stormrider (ground and air forces: ground matches no anti role, air gives anti-air); database entries: Missile Squad (vehicles and aircraft), Predator (any vehicle or structure), Riflemen (trained for anti-infantry fighting, which is also a label for roles.secondary step 1). Text tied to one of two weapons counts only for that weapon at roles.secondary step 3 (the Firehawk's air-to-air missiles; its bombs are the other load).
  - Weak: the Predator (poor against infantry, exposed to aircraft), Beam Cannon (not meant for attacks on armour), Riflemen (database: never against heavy armour). The Pitbull's too-light-for-a-straight-fight names no target; the Orca's database line that it cannot engage aircraft is a can_target fact, not weak text.
  - Target words: vehicles, armour, tanks and armoured or light vehicles mean armour; infantry, soldiers, troops and squads mean infantry; aircraft and air mean air. Structures, buildings, bases, installations and garrisons match none of the three anti roles. Ground, land and surface targets match none either.
- **Step 4 bonus from the game data: yes, from weapon damage scalars.** A weapon's damage can carry its own multiplier against a kind of target (`DamageScalarDetails` in `GlobalData/Weapon.xml`; the infoboxes show it as, for example, a 200% scalar against aircraft). Stock weapons with one above full damage against a whole kind: the Raider Buggy's gun, the Gun Walker and the Shard Walker (double against aircraft), the Pitbull's and Stealth Tank's rockets (half again against aircraft), the Mechapede's disc segment (four times against aircraft), the Ravager's shards (more than double against vehicles; the same shards arm the Mechapede's shard segment and the Eradicator's Ravager hardpoint). The Attack Bike's rockets reach a bonus against aircraft only with Tiberium Core Missiles. Bonuses against civilian buildings (most Scrin weapons) and structures (flamethrowers) match no anti role.
  - Target-side shares above full damage exist too (`GlobalData/Armor.xml`), but only for a few armour sets: Gun does half again to Missile Squad and Militant Rocket soldiers and double to Fanatics; Cannon does half again to the Shatterer, Zone Shatterer, Slingshot and Flame Tank and a little more to the Titan, Attack Bike and Seeker; Rocket does a little more to the Attack Bike. Proposal for the lead: these are counters to those units, not a bonus against infantry or armour as a kind (the reference rifle soldier and the Predator take full damage at most), so they give no step 4 role; use them in matchups. Read literally, every Gun weapon would turn anti-infantry and every Cannon weapon anti-armour.
  - Shares below full damage (several machine guns do three quarters to infantry) are never a bonus.
- **Subfaction copies.** A copy shares its base unit's paragraph unless the Kane's Wrath manual gives it its own (the Steel Talons, ZOCOM, Black Hand, Marked of Kane, Reaper-17 and Traveler-59 sections). The base paragraph counts for a copy only where the copy keeps the part it describes: the Black Hand Commando has no stealth, and the Black Hand Specter does not cloak (the KW manual's own note).
- **Not official.** The UnitBox `role`, `useguns` and `usearmor` fields and the prose; StrategyWiki's Tiberium Wars unit pages (role fields and Counters sections; kind guide); CNCNZ's unit pages, which reword the manual and add their own lines (kind guide); EVA and unit voice lines quoted on unit pages (the Predator page's EVA line about Nod vehicles and structures is mission dialogue, not a unit description).
- **Official site.** Whether EA's 2007 site had unit profiles is unchecked: web.archive.org reset every connection from this session, and archive.org's lookup found no snapshot of the address tried (commandandconquer.com/cnc3). GameSpot's designer diaries answered 403.

### Tiberium Wars with Kane's Wrath (`cnc3`)

Written in batch R2 preparation, before any `cnc3` unit is coded, for Kane's Wrath patch 1.02 in skirmish and multiplayer. Sources: the Tiberium Wars manual (gameplay pages: PDF pages 8 to 11, printed 12 to 19; link under Official role lines) and the Kane's Wrath manual (Complete Controls, printed page 2, and its unit sections); the Command & Conquer Wiki pages named below (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/<Title>, read through the API); and EA's released Kane's Wrath XML (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Modding_Support/main/Kanes%20Wrath/Xml/<path>), which matches patch 1.02 on every value checked (see the research notes).

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): every unit. Move and attack by right-click, attack move, assault move (also attacks buildings on the way), reverse move (backs up; the manual pairs it with armour facing), force move (drives through enemies, so tanks run over infantry), force attack, formation move (the group keeps to its slowest member), stop, scatter, waypoints, planning mode (queued orders and patrols), rally points, and four stances: aggressive, guard (the default), hold ground and hold fire; a production building's stance passes to what it builds (Tiberium Wars manual, PDF pages 9 and 11; Kane's Wrath manual, Complete Controls; [Stance](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stance); XML `GlobalData/Stances.xml`). No retreat or reinforce order. The ability buttons (Ctrl with A, S, D or F) belong to each unit: record them on it.
- **Veterancy** (`earn-veterancy`): every unit that fights, except those below. Three ranks, veteran, elite and heroic, earned from the value of the damage a unit deals rather than from kills; crates can also promote ([Veterancy](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Veterancy), Tiberium Wars section; Tiberium Wars manual, Unit Veterancy, PDF page 9).
  - What ranks add (XML `GlobalData/AttributeModifier.xml`): more damage and more health at each rank (patch 1.02 raised the elite step to a quarter more damage and two fifths more health; [Kane's Wrath patch 1.02](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Kane%27s_Wrath_patch_1.02)); at heroic, double the firing rate and steady self-healing (`BaseObjects/BaseVehicle.xml` and `BaseInfantry.xml`, switched on by the heroic rank), with red tracers (manual). The Veterancy page also claims more speed, and more range at heroic; the 1.02 modifiers give neither, so leave both out. Bands use the unranked unit; no armour model, no ability.
  - **Cannot rank up** (no levels in `GlobalData/ExperienceLevels.xml`): the Nod and Scrin harvesters (subfaction ones included), the three MCVs, Surveyor, Emissary, Explorer, the GDI and ZOCOM Engineers, the Assimilator, Fanatics and Traveler-59 Cultists, and the Ox and Carryall. The GDI side's harvesters do rank up (the armed GDI and ZOCOM Rocket Harvesters, and the Steel Talons Heavy Harvester with its garrison pod). Fanatics and Cultists say so in weaknesses; the unarmed ones only in notes.
  - **Built ranked**: Black Hand flame units arrive veteran (Veterancy page) and Black Hand Commandos heroic ([Black Hand](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Black_Hand)); units summoned by powers arrive veteran (GDI Airborne by the Armory page; Zone Raider drop pods and Shock Pods by the Kane's Wrath manual). Stock values exclude veterancy: band the unranked unit and say in notes how it arrives.
- **Infantry squads** (no pattern): most infantry are bought and commanded as one squad. The squad moves at its own speed, and each member's figure is a little higher so the group keeps formation (XML locomotor sets). Lost members are not replaced, except by the GDI Armory (repair, below).
- **Infantry suppression and cover** (no pattern, not an armour model): human infantry under heavy fire go prone, crawling at about a quarter of their speed but taking less damage, and force move stands them up; stronger weapons suppress more ([Infantry Suppression](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Infantry_Suppression); manual PDF page 11; XML modifier `Modifier_Test_Suppression`). Never suppressed: Marked of Kane cyborgs, Fanatics and Scrin infantry (page and manual); the XML gives no suppression to Zone Troopers and Zone Raiders either. The manual calls Grenadiers hard to suppress. Infantry next to civilian buildings or big obstacles kneel in cover, tougher and almost impossible to suppress (manual). Leave all of it off; mention it in armour.notes where it matters. The Confessor Cabal and the Purifier suppress nearby enemy infantry and lift their own (page; Kane's Wrath manual): record that on those two. The Voice of Kane statue does the same and stays off.
- **Garrisons** (`carry-passengers`, recorded on the building, which is not researched): infantry squads can enter civilian buildings, up to three squads, and fire out with protection and extra reach; a badly damaged building throws them out, and a garrisoned building cannot be repaired ([Garrisoning](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning), Tiberium Wars section; manual PDF page 9; Intelligence Database, Garrisoning). Range bands use the soldier in the open.
  - Cannot garrison: Zone Troopers and Zone Raiders; Scrin infantry, apart from Buzzers (which enter a building to attack those inside) and Cultists. Say so in weaknesses where it matters.
  - Clearing a garrison belongs to the weapon that does it; name it in that weapon's summary. In the XML these clear garrisons: the Grenadier's grenades, the Black Hand's and Black Disciple's flamethrowers, the Flame Tank, the Avatar's upgraded flamer, the Purifier, the Redeemer's flame and Tiberium turrets, the MARV's grenadier hardpoint, the Firehawk's bombs, Buzzers, the Corrupter, the Tiberium Trooper, and the Saboteur's booby trap.
  - Riflemen dig their own foxholes (Dig In): their ability.
- **Transports** (universal keys: get in, get out, Evacuate; one seat passive per carrier, see Paired entries):
  - One squad: the APC, Mobile Repair Transport, Hammerhead, Behemoth and Heavy Harvester; two, three once deployed into a bunker: the Reckoner (XML `HordeTransportContain`; Garrisoning page; Kane's Wrath manual). Riders fire out of the APC (manual; the database adds that a Missile Squad inside gives it missiles), the Hammerhead and the deployed Reckoner (Garrisoning page): passenger-firing seats, `passenger-sets-weapon`. Check the others on their pages.
  - Riders die with the vehicle, except in the Reckoner (XML `KillPassengersOnDeath`): on_death.notes.
  - The epic units take infantry for good, each squad adding a weapon hardpoint, and cannot let them out: the MARV four squads, the Redeemer two, the Eradicator three (Garrisoning page; [Epic unit](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Epic_unit); Kane's Wrath manual): `passenger-sets-weapon`.
  - Whether a seat is a squad or a soldier is open (research notes).
- **Call for transport** (no pattern; leave off): GDI (all three versions), Nod and Marked of Kane infantry and light and medium vehicles can summon a V-35 Ox or a Carryall that lifts them anywhere on the map, for a fee and on a long recharge, once an Airfield or Air Tower stands ([Call for transport](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Call_for_transport); Intelligence Database; XML `SpecialPowerTemplates.xml`). Not: Black Hand (no Air Tower), the Scrin (they teleport), and the heavy units (Mammoth, Juggernaut, Behemoth, Titan, Avatar, Purifier, Flame and Stealth Tanks, Reckoner, Rig, epic units), harvesters, MCVs and aircraft; `GlobalData/LogicCommandSet.xml` lists exactly who has the button. A unit without it needs nothing. The Ox and Carryall come only this way and are not researched.
- **Repair, healing and rearming** (no pattern; leave off):
  - Every vehicle factory (War Factory, Warp Sphere, Reclamator Hub, Redeemer Engineering Facility, Warp Chasm) and aircraft building (Airfield, Air Tower, Gravity Stabilizer) keeps three repair drones that mend nearby vehicles or aircraft; Scrin drones also heal infantry; the Scrin Reconstruction Drones power drops more for a while ([Repair drone (Tiberium Wars)](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Repair_drone_(Tiberium_Wars)); [Reconstruction drones](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Reconstruction_drones)). The Rig's Battle Base and the Mobile Repair Transport carry drones of their own: `repair-allies` on those two.
  - The GDI and ZOCOM Armory heals squads sent inside and replaces lost members, the only thing in the game that restores members ([Armory](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Armory)). Steel Talons have no Armory.
  - Buildings are repaired in repair mode; engineers repair buildings and bridges (their own ability).
  - The Orca, ZOCOM Orca, Firehawk and Vertigo reload their weapons only at an Airfield or Air Tower (XML weapons that reload at base; Kane's Wrath adds smaller pads that rearm and repair but do not build, the GDI Combat Support Airfield and the Nod Air Support Tower): resource `limited-ammo`, and leave the trip off. The Hammerhead never needs to (Kane's Wrath manual); the Venom and the Scrin aircraft reload by themselves (XML). Most aircraft also need a free landing pad on their building before they can be built (infobox `req`; an Airfield keeps four aircraft, Intelligence Database), so how many fly grows with buildings: availability stays open.
- **Husks** (on_death `wreck`): the Juggernaut, Behemoth, Avatar, Purifier, Annihilator Tripod and Reaper Tripod leave a husk when destroyed. An Engineer, Combat Engineer, Saboteur or Assimilator of either side can bring it back into the fight; left alone it falls apart, and heavy and epic units can crush it ([Husk](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Husk); the four engineers' pages; manual PDF page 10). The Titan, Gun Walker, Redeemer and Eradicator leave none. The engineers' capture ability links `recover-wreck` beside `capture-structure`; the Saboteur's booby trap on a husk is its own ability.
- **Crushing** (mobility trait `crush`, not an ability): a unit runs over another when its crusher level is above the other's crushable level (XML `CrusherInfo`; many infoboxes give both as crush and crushable; the manual's force move). Ordinary vehicles crush basic infantry and can themselves be crushed by the heavy crushers below (`BaseObjects/BaseVehicle.xml`).
  - Not crushers: the APC, Pitbull, Wolverine, Mobile Repair Transport, Attack Bike, Raider Buggy, Beam Cannon, Seeker, Explorer and Scrin harvester.
  - Heavy crushers, which also run over heavy infantry and light vehicles: the Mammoth, Juggernaut, Behemoth, Titan, Avatar, Purifier and both Tripods (the manual says so for the Mammoth and Tripod, the Kane's Wrath manual for the Titan). The MARV, Eradicator and Redeemer (its infobox gives the same top level) crush every non-epic unit.
  - Heavy infantry escape ordinary vehicles (Zone Troopers, Zone Raiders, the Enlightened, Shock Troopers, Ravagers); both Commandos, the Mastermind, Prodigy and Buzzers can be crushed only by epic units. Proposal: `immune:crush` in strengths only for that second group, with the epic exception in the reason; for the first group, say in armour.notes which vehicles can still crush them. A crusher smaller than large still gets the trait, with the size break in atypical.
- **Armour facing** (armour model `directional`): tanks and other armoured vehicles take more damage from the side and much more from behind (manual, Armour Facing, PDF page 11). The XML (`GlobalData/Armor.xml`, side and rear scalars) gives it, a tenth more from the side and half again from behind, to the Predator, Mammoth, Juggernaut, Behemoth, Pitbull, APC, Mobile Repair Transport, Shatterer, Zone Shatterer, Slingshot, Rig, GDI MCV, Surveyor, Avatar and its subfaction copies, Beam Cannon, Scorpion, Specter, Reckoner, Flame Tank, Raider Buggy, Stealth Tank, Devourer, Explorer, Eradicator and Redeemer, with a smaller rear step on the Titan and MARV. Code directional on each, citing its armour set. The Seeker, Gun Walker, Shard Walker, both Tripods, Corrupter, Wolverine, Attack Bike, harvesters, aircraft and infantry have none. The data also gives facing to the Nod Commando and the Saboteur: code it there with an uncertain entry, since the manual speaks only of vehicles.
- **Tiberium** (map hazard; leave off): standing in a Tiberium field hurts infantry (XML `TiberiumCrystalWeapon`), except Scrin infantry, Zone Troopers and Zone Raiders, and Marked of Kane Tiberium Troopers (its exclusion list): `immune:toxic` in strengths for those. Upgrades protect Militants, Confessors and Fanatics (Tiberium Infusion) and ZOCOM infantry (Tiberium Field Suits): notes only. Scrin infantry and harvesters heal near Tiberium (XML `HEALED_BY_TIBERIUM`; both manuals): armour.notes, not self-repair. Blue Tiberium is worth more (manual). The Scrin Infestation power and Overlord's Wrath seed hurting fields: off.
- **Upgrades** (see Paired entries): researched at a building, an upgrade reaches every unit of its type at once, those already fighting included (manual, Upgrading Technology, PDF page 8). So a weapon or ability an upgrade adds links `upgrade-in-field`; an upgrade that only changes numbers goes in notes. A swapped weapon (railguns, laser capacitors, shard launchers, Tiberium Core Missiles, charged particle beams) is an acquired weapon only when its family or damage changes; otherwise name it in the stock weapon's summary.
- **Side-wide powers and buildings** (left off every unit; none gives a named unit type a new button, so no ability has source commander-power):
  - GDI: Ion Cannon, Orbital Strike, Shockwave Artillery, Radar Scan, Sonic Repulsion Field, Supersonic Air Strike, Railgun Accelerator (Steel Talons; faster fire with self-damage for railgun units in an area: a number change, so name it in their railgun summaries); call-ins GDI Airborne, Zone Trooper and Zone Raider drop pods, Orca strike, Bloodhounds, Sharpshooter Team.
  - Nod: Nuclear Missile, Cloaking Field (cloaks vehicles and buildings in an area, not infantry), Decoy Army, Radar Jamming Missile, Catalyst Missile, Tiberium Vapour Bomb, Seed Tiberium, Mine Drop, Master Computer Countermeasures (ends EMP), Laser Fencing, Power Signature Scan, Decoy Temple, Magnetic Mines, Tiberium Vein Detonation, the Voice of Kane statue; call-ins Shadow Strike Team and Redemption (fallen Militants rise as Awakened).
  - Scrin: Rift, Wormhole, Temporal Wormhole, Lightning Spike, The Swarm, Tiberium Vibration Scan, Stasis Shield, Phase Field, Ichor Seed, Infestation, Overlord's Wrath, Reconstruction Drones; call-in Shock Pods.
  - Sources: the wiki's support-power categories for both games (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Tiberium_Wars_support_powers and the Kane's Wrath one), [Railgun accelerator](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Railgun_accelerator), [Master computer countermeasures](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Master_computer_countermeasures), the Kane's Wrath manual. Mention an effect in notes where it shapes a matchup. Call-in units are not researched.
- **Stealth and detection** (per unit): code each unit's own cloak and detection with `cloak` and the stealth and detector traits ([Stealth](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth), Tiberium Wars section, lists both sides). Units hidden only by the Cloaking Field, a Disruption Tower or Disruption Pods get no cloak of their own; the Vertigo records its pods. Many base defences detect, which belongs to no unit. Detection bought with an upgrade (Scanner Packs) is notes.
- **EMP** (no pattern for the state): EMP grenades (a Grenadier upgrade), the Raider Buggy's EMP Burst and the EMP Blast of the Awakened and Enlightened stop vehicles and buildings for a while; a building hit by EMP stops counting as a prerequisite until it recovers (manual PDF page 10; Kane's Wrath manual). The Steel Talons' Adaptive Armor and the Scrin's Attenuated Forcefields protect against it (Kane's Wrath manual). Record each EMP on the unit that fires it; protection bought by upgrade goes in notes.
- **Mind control**: since patch 1.02 the Mastermind, Prodigy and Cultists cannot take over epic units or commandos (Kane's Wrath patch 1.02 page): `immune:mind-control` in their strengths.
- **Damaged vehicles slow down** (no pattern): most vehicle locomotors fall to three quarters of their speed when badly damaged, a few to half (XML `MaxSpeedDamaged`). Speed bands use full health.
- **Crates** (a multiplayer option; picking one up is a universal key): only good effects; random ones in skirmish and multiplayer give money, a rank, a damage or armour boost or healing, never units ([Crate](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Crate), Tiberium Wars section; manual PDF page 10). Leave them off. Barrels on maps explode when shot (manual).
- **Fog, radar and power** (no pattern): fog of war is always on in skirmish, and support powers cannot be aimed into it ([Fog of war](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Fog_of_war)); low power takes the radar and base defences off line and slows building (manual, PDF page 8). Repair drones vanish while their building lacks power (Repair drone page). No unit depends on power, so nothing is `depend-on-relay`.
- **Engineers and capture**: not game-wide. The Engineer, Combat Engineer, Saboteur and Assimilator capture enemy buildings and husks and repair friendly buildings and bridges (manual; Intelligence Database; their pages): `capture-structure`, with `recover-wreck` for husks. Taking a neutral tech building (Tiberium Spike, EMP Control Center) is not `capture-structure`: name it in the summary; what it gives its owner is side-wide.
- **Build limits** (availability `unique`; say so in tier.basis): one at a time for the GDI Commando, Nod Commando (Black Hand: two), Mastermind, Prodigy and Mothership, and one epic unit per player, the MARV, Redeemer or Eradicator (XML `MaxSimultaneousOfType`; Epic unit page; Black Hand page; [Mothership](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Mothership)).

notes.other_notes:
- **Version and mode.** Code every unit as Kane's Wrath patch 1.02 plays in skirmish and multiplayer, for all nine factions. Global Conquest (Kane's Wrath's turn-based mode, with strike forces and meta-unit hardpoints) is out of scope; leave its effects out (the Redeemer's unrest bonus there, for one).
- **EA's Kane's Wrath XML is the 1.02 game data; use it.** EA's modding release https://github.com/electronicarts/CnC_Modding_Support holds the game's XML. Unit files are at `Kanes Wrath/Xml/<faction folder>/Units/<file>.xml` (folders GDI, NOD, Alien, SteelTalons, ZOCOM, BlackHand, MarkedOfKane, Reaper17, Traveler59); shared data is in `GlobalData/` (Weapon.xml, Armor.xml, Locomotor.xml, ExperienceLevels.xml, AttributeModifier.xml, SpecialPowerTemplates.xml, LogicCommandSet.xml, upgrade.xml) and defaults in `BaseObjects/`. Read files through https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Modding_Support/main/Kanes%20Wrath/Xml/<path>; github.com folder pages opened only through WebFetch. `Tiberium Wars/Xml/` in the same repository is the Tiberium Wars 1.09 data.
  - Why it is 1.02: every 1.02 change checked is in it (all harvesters, the Specter and the Shard Walker at their 1.02 prices; the elite rank's 1.02 bonus; the Mammoth's 1.02 health; the Hammerhead's, Avatar's and Devourer's 1.02 reach; the Shadow Team's 1.02 speeds), and `GlobalData/TheVersion.xml` reads 114.
  - Cite a file by its raw URL as kind official (EA's own release of its data), with a note naming the keys read; the copy-check can read it. Proposal: where it and the wiki disagree, the XML wins, with an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree. The only disagreement found so far is the Scorpion's price.
  - Where things are: price and build time in the `GameObject` attributes `BuildCost` and `BuildTime`; speed in the `LocomotorSet` with condition NORMAL; sight in `VisionRange` and `ShroudClearingRange`; reach in the weapon's `AttackRange` (Weapon.xml); damage category and per-target scalars in the weapon's nuggets; armour in the unit's `ArmorSet` and Armor.xml (per-category shares, side and rear scalars); requirements in `GameDependency`; build limits in `MaxSimultaneousOfType`; crushing in `CrusherInfo`; carried squads in the `*Contain` modules.
  - Internal names that differ from the game's: NODRaiderTank is the Scorpion Tank and NODScorpionBuggy the Raider Buggy; NODMobileArtillery the Specter; NODBunkerTruck the Reckoner; NODTechAssemblyPlant the Tech Lab; GDIAAScout the Slingshot; GDISonicTank the Shatterer and ZOCOMImprovedSonicTank the Zone Shatterer; GDIMedicalBay the Armory, GDIArmory the Tech Center and GDIAirTower the Airfield; SteelTalonsRepairAPC the Mobile Repair Transport; MOKCyborgInfantry the Awakened and MarkedOfKaneImprovedCyborgInfantry the Enlightened; BlackHandCustomWarmech the Purifier; AlienStalker the Ravager; AlienRazorDrones the Disintegrators; AlienBlinkMastermind the Prodigy; AlienMillipede the Mechapede; AlienMCV the Drone Ship; AlienControlCenter the Nerve Center; AlienStatisChamber the Stasis Chamber; AlienReactor, as a requirement, the Technology Assembler.
  - The data also holds files a subfaction never fields in skirmish (SteelTalonsPredator, SteelTalonsZoneTrooperSquad, ZOCOMJuggernaught, BlackHandCyborgInfantrySquad, MarkedOfKaneMilitantSquad, among others). Take who builds what from the subfaction pages and the Kane's Wrath manual, not from the XML.
- **Settled: infantry speeds and versions.** The infobox `landspeed` of every infantry squad is the squad's own speed in the data (its `LocomotorSet`, for example the Rifleman squad 57 and the Militant squad 43), and the Kane's Wrath 1.02 and Tiberium Wars 1.09 files give the same figure for every squad both games share, apart from the Shadow Team (Kane's Wrath 90 on foot and 120 gliding, after patch 1.02; Tiberium Wars 80 and 100). Each soldier's own figure is a little higher (rifleman 62, militant 48) so the squad keeps formation. So no wiki infantry figure belongs to another version, and the Rifleman-Militant gap is design, not a patch mix: Militants are simply slower. Patch 1.05 sped up named infantry and the APC by about a fifth (the Black Hand slightly more, the Disintegrators slightly less) and left out the Nod Commando, Zone Troopers, Fanatics, Shock Troopers and Shadow Team ([Tiberium Wars patch 1.05](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Tiberium_Wars_patch_1.05)); although Kane's Wrath was built on the code from before that patch ([Kane's Wrath patch 1.01](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Kane%27s_Wrath_patch_1.01)), its data carries the faster figures.
- **Settled: the Devourer's price.** 1,600 credits is right for Kane's Wrath: the Kane's Wrath XML gives 1600 (build time 16), the Tiberium Wars 1.09 file 1400 (14), and CNCNZ's pages agree with each (https://cncnz.com/games/tiberium-wars/scrin-units/ and https://cncnz.com/games/kanes-wrath/scrin-units/). The change came with the expansion itself: neither Kane's Wrath patch touches the price; 1.02 only shortened its reach a little (the changelog on the [Devourer tank](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Devourer_tank) page; the [patch 1.02 page](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Kane%27s_Wrath_patch_1.02)).
- **Settled: what Kane's Wrath 1.02 changed in costs and upgrades** (Kane's Wrath patch 1.02 page; every price below is also in the XML):
  - Unit prices: every harvester 1,600 (build 16 seconds), Specter 1,500 (15), Shard Walker 800 (8); the Obelisk of Light, a building, 2,000.
  - Ability prices: Orca sensor pod 100, APC minefield 300, Vertigo disruption pod 300, Saboteur booby trap 100.
  - GDI upgrades: Pitbull mortar 1,000; AP Ammo 2,000 with a longer 60-second research; Hardpoints 60 seconds; Scanner Packs 500 and 15 seconds, range bonus doubled to a fifth; Autoinjectors 1,000 and 30 seconds; Stratofighter boosters 1,000 and 30 seconds; Composite Armor 1,500 and 45 seconds; Tiberium Field Suits 1,000 and 30 seconds; Railguns 4,000; Adaptive Armor 1,000.
  - Nod upgrades: Tiberium Infusion 1,000 and 30 seconds; Laser Capacitors 2,500 and 75 seconds; Black Disciples 1,000 and 30 seconds; Tiberium Core Missiles raised to 2,500 and 75 seconds; Supercharged Particle Beams 3,000; Dozer Blades armour bonus cut from a quarter to 15 percent.

  - Powers (not researched): Railgun Accelerator, Orbital Strike, Supersonic Air Strike, Cloaking Field (less damage to infantry), Power Signature Scan, Decoy Temple, Redemption, Radar Jamming Missile, Tiberium Vibration Scan, Infestation.

- **Speed bands.** speed_raw = the unit's NORMAL locomotor speed (the infobox `landspeed` or `airspeed`) ÷ 57, at full health, unsuppressed, before upgrades (Advanced Articulators, Traveler Engines, Cybernetic Legs and the like). Squads use the squad figure. Aircraft use their air speed; the Shadow Team's glider, Zone Trooper and Zone Raider jump jets, blink packs and teleports are abilities, not speeds.
- **Sight bands.** Use the shroud-clearing figure against the Rifleman squad's 400: the infobox's second sight line, or `ShroudClearingRange` in the XML when the infobox has none (the Missile and Grenadier squads, Venom, Gun Walker, Seeker, Devourer, Corrupter, Annihilator and Reaper Tripods, Eradicator, Mechapede, Shard Walker and others). Never the vision figure (see the registry finding). The Vertigo's infobox says only far; take its XML figure.
- **Range bands.** Reach is the weapon's `AttackRange` (the infobox `range`); the reference rifle reaches 260. The off-screen test compares a weapon with the unit's own shroud-clearing figure. Artillery outranges its own sight and needs spotters (Sniper Teams for the Juggernaut, the Shadow Team's beacon for the Specter): name that in the weapon summary.
- **Damage categories: the batch note's named exceptions are too few (proposal for the lead).** The note names only the Avatar, Obelisk and Tripod lasers, the Shatterer's sonic beam and flamethrowers. Many other lasers, beams, plasma, sonic and Tiberium weapons carry a plain category in their infoboxes, so step 4 would map them as: the Nod Commando's laser pistols Sniper (kinetic); the Redeemer's and Purifier's lasers, the Devourer's laser cannon, the Awakened's and Enlightened's particle beams, the Invader fighters' and the Eradicator's plasma, and the Zone Raider's and MARV's sonic shells Cannon (armour-piercing); the Beam Cannon's particle beam Grenade (explosive); the Venom's and Raider Buggy's upgrade lasers and the Gun Walker's plasma Gun (kinetic); the Seeker's discs, the Shock Trooper's proton cannon, the Stormrider's plasma and the Disintegrators' plasma cutter Rocket (armour-piercing); the Devastator's plasma discs Grenade (explosive); the Tiberium Trooper's and Corrupter's Tiberium sprays Grenade (explosive). Proposal for step 3: every laser, particle beam, proton or disintegrator beam and plasma weapon is energy; every sonic weapon (Shatterer and Zone Shatterer, the Zone Raider's and ZOCOM Orca's sonic shells, the MARV's cannon) is sonic; every flamethrower is fire; the Tiberium sprays are toxic. Transport's requires asks for two or more seats, and no rule says whether a seat is a squad or a soldier. verdicts.claim: Intelligence Database: the wiki transcribes it; the tabs and entries are as listed; there are no KW entries for the Titan, Wolverine, MRT, Zone Shatterer, ZOCOM Orca, Reckoner, Mantis, Ravager or Mechapede; the other TW Scrin units have no entries

verdicts.evidence: https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Intelligence_Database (API wikitext), sections checked one by one.

verdicts.claim: Roles step 1: the list of paragraphs that name a role is complete (Pitbull, Attack Bike, Orca, Seeker, Sniper Team, Juggernaut, Specter, Behemoth, Missile Squad, Mantis, Shard Walker, Ravager, APC, Reckoner, MRT, engineers, Saboteur, harvesters)
verdicts.reason: Several paragraphs and names that carry a label or alias are left out.
verdicts.evidence: UC text = TW manual PDF 17: the Rig is called a heavy support vehicle and carries repair drones. KW manual p.16 calls the Wolverine a perfect scout unit. The Vertigo Bomber's name (TW manual PDF 21) contains 'bomber', a siege alias in data/vocab/roles.json. The Sniper Team's name contains 'sniper', a marksman alias.
verdicts.correction: Add: support for the Rig (heavy support vehicle with repair drones); scout for the Wolverine (KW manual; subject to scout's requires); siege for the Vertigo Bomber (its name, and the Intel DB calls it a stealth bomber; its bombs meet siege's drop requirement); marksman for the Sniper Team (its name).

verdicts.claim: The Sniper Team names scout at step 1 through 'trained in reconnaissance'
verdicts.reason: The unit names two roles, not one. Neither has a target, so step 1 gives nothing; step 3 then gives marksman for its long-range sniper rifle. The same paragraph also calls it deadly against infantry, which the strong-against list omits.
verdicts.evidence: UC text (= TW PDF 16): the Sniper Team paragraph (kills most infantry from long range; reconnaissance; artillery target spotting). data/vocab/roles.json: marksman aliases sniper, sharpshooter; scout aliases recon, reconnaissance, spotter. docs/fields.md roles.primary step 1: if no remaining role has a bonus, go on.
verdicts.correction: Sniper Team: its name names marksman, and its paragraph names scout (reconnaissance, spotting). No target, so step 1 gives nothing and step 3 gives marksman. Its paragraph and its Intel DB entry also make it strong against infantry.

verdicts.claim: The APC and the Reckoner name transport ('armoured personnel carrier', 'the Reckoner APC')
verdicts.reason: The APC's manual paragraph never says personnel carrier: it only says infantry ride it safely and fire from inside. 'Armored Personnel Carrier' appears only in its Intel DB entry and as the meaning of its abbreviated name. Transport's aliases do not include 'APC', so reading 'APC' as 'personnel carrier' is a judgment for the lead. Both units stay subject to passengers >= 2, and the APC holds one squad.
verdicts.evidence: UC text, APC paragraph (= TW PDF 17). KW manual p.18, Reckoner paragraph. Intel DB APC entry. data/vocab/roles.json transport aliases: troop transport, troop carrier, personnel carrier.
verdicts.correction: Transport: the Reckoner ('Reckoner APC') and the APC, the latter only through its name and its Intel DB entry, if the lead lets the abbreviation count. Both are subject to passengers >= 2.

verdicts.claim: The Ravager names raider (hit-and-run attacks)
verdicts.reason: The KW paragraph does name hit-and-run. But raider requires speed >= fast, and the Ravager squad moves at 75, which is 1.32 times the reference 57 and so in the medium band. Step 1 therefore skips raider.
verdicts.evidence: KW manual p.24, Ravager paragraph. Kanes Wrath/Xml/Alien/Units/AlienStalkerSquad.xml speed 75 (member 80). Wiki Ravager landspeed 75. data/vocab/speed-bands.json: fast means over 1.5 times the reference.
verdicts.correction: The Ravager's paragraph names raider, but raider's requires fail (speed 75 = 1.32x, medium), so step 1 gives nothing for it.

verdicts.claim: Step 1 also names support for the MRT, engineer for the Engineer and Combat Engineer, infiltrator for the Saboteur and logistics for every harvester
verdicts.reason: Confirmed, with two cautions. The MRT's name contains 'Transport' and its paragraph mentions standard APC functionality, so under the count-soldiers seat reading transport also survives and step 1 goes on. The Engineer's, Saboteur's and Assimilator's paragraphs also say they repair buildings ('repair' is a support alias). That is skipped only if building repair fails support's requires (repair-allies: repair vehicles or heal soldiers).
verdicts.evidence: KW manual p.16 (MRT). UC text: Engineer, Saboteur and Assimilator paragraphs. data/pattern-registry.json repair-allies summary.

verdicts.claim: These paragraphs name no role: Rifleman Squad, Predator, Mammoth, Titan, Grenadier, Commando, Zone Trooper, Zone Raider, Scorpion, Stealth Tank, Flame Tank, Avatar, Black Hand, Militants, Venom, Stormrider, Annihilator, Devourer, Gun Walker, Awakened, Enlightened, Confessor Cabal, Purifier (buffer has no alias)
verdicts.reason: The manual paragraphs carry no label or alias, and buffer has no aliases. However, the Intel DB gives several of these units labels that count at roles.secondary step 1, and the notes miss them.

Intel DB: the InOps Nod Aircraft entry calls the Venom a VTOL scout; the New Nod Flame Tank entry calls it a classic anti-infantry weapon system; the Flame Weapons entry calls flamethrowers anti-infantry weapons; the GDI Zone Raider entry says its role became a first-response scouting unit for Red Zones; the GDI Hammerhead entry calls it an assault/transport hybrid.
verdicts.correction: Keep the list for step 1. For roles.secondary step 1 add the Intel DB labels: Venom scout, Flame Tank (and Black Hand flamers) anti-infantry, Zone Raider scout, Hammerhead transport (subject to passengers >= 2).

verdicts.claim: Strong-against list (Commando, Raider Buggy, Zone Trooper, Militant Rocket Squad, Attack Bike, Slingshot, Venom, Gun Walker, Reaper Tripod, ZOCOM Orca, Shatterer, Stormrider; database: Missile Squad, Predator, Riflemen), with the Firehawk's air-to-air missiles counting only for that weapon
verdicts.reason: Every listed item is confirmed, but many official strong lines are missing.
verdicts.evidence: UC text (= the 2007 paragraphs): the Sniper Team kills most infantry; Black Hand flamethrowers incinerate enemy squads; Buzzers cut through flesh and light armour; Disintegrators decimate vehicles; Shock Troopers can attack armoured vehicles head-on; the Corrupter is devastating to humans. KW manual p.16: the Combat Engineer is good at taking down enemy Engineers. verdicts.correction: Add strong vs infantry: Sniper Team, Black Hand, Corrupter (humans), Combat Engineer (enemy Engineers). Strong vs armour: Disintegrators, Shock Troopers, Stealth Tank (DB), Avatar (DB). Strong vs infantry and light armour: Buzzers. Anti-air labels: Pitbull (Mortars text) and Slingshot (DB).

verdicts.claim: Weak-against list: Predator (infantry, aircraft), Beam Cannon (armour), Riflemen (DB: heavy armour). The Pitbull's 'too light for direct combat' names no target, and the Orca's DB line is a can_target fact.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Role trap: the Stealth Tank has no official strength, so step 4 gives anti-air from its rockets' 150% against aircraft
verdicts.reason: The Intel DB Stealth Tank entry (Kane's Arsenal tab) says its missiles work against vehicles and structures. So step 4 has two targets: armour from official text and air from the data scalar. If the lead finds the two sizes incomparable, the tie rule takes the one official text names first, which is anti-armour.
verdicts.evidence: https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Intelligence_Database, section Stealth Tank. https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth_tank_(Tiberium_Wars) airattack +150% vs aircraft. docs/fields.md roles.primary step 4, last sentence.
verdicts.correction: Stealth Tank: official text (Intel DB) says strong against vehicles; data gives 150% against aircraft. By the tie rule, anti-armour primary with anti-air for secondary, plus an uncertain entry; or the lead rules on comparing a text strength with a data bonus.

verdicts.claim: Step 4 data bonuses: Buggy, Gun Walker and Shard Walker 200% vs aircraft; Pitbull and Stealth Tank 150%; the Mechapede's stock disc segment 400%; Ravager shards 225% vs vehicles (also the Mechapede shard segment and the Eradicator hardpoint); the Attack Bike only with Tiberium Core Missiles; flamethrowers have a bonus against structures
verdicts.reason: The figures are right, but: (1) the Mantis rockets also do 150% vs aircraft (200% with Tiberium Core Missiles) and are missing; (2) Mechapede segments are bought one at a time through its Add Weapon Segment ability, so the disc segment is not stock; (3) the 150% vs structures sits only on the Flame Tank's flamers (and the Avatar's flamer once upgraded), not on the Black Hand troopers' or the Purifier's flamers; (4) the Redeemer's rocket hardpoint (150% vs aircraft) matches the Eradicator hardpoint the notes do list.
verdicts.evidence: GlobalData/Weapon.xml: BlackHandTankTankRocketWarhead 150% AIRCRAFT, BlackHandTankTankRocketTibCoreWarhead 200%, NODWarmechRocketWarhead 150%. Wiki infoboxes: Mantis airattack +150%; Flame tank +150% vs buildings; Black Hand and Purifier have no structure scalar; Redeemer rocket turret +150% vs aircraft. KW manual pp.24 and 27: Add Weapon Segment(s).
verdicts.correction: Add the Mantis (150%, 200% with TCM). Call the Mechapede's segments bought parts, not stock. Limit the structure bonus to the Flame Tank family's flamers.

verdicts.claim: Basic orders: right-click move and attack, attack move, assault move (also hits buildings), reverse, force move (tanks overrun infantry), force attack, formation move (slowest member), stop, scatter, waypoints, planning mode and patrols, rally points; four stances with Guard as default, inherited from the factory; no retreat or reinforce order

verdicts.reason: In the 1.02 data heroic adds no damage over elite. It adds health, fire rate and suppression resistance. The manual says heroic units hit harder than elite, so the manual and the data disagree.

verdicts.correction: Veteran +15% damage +20% health; elite +25%/+40% (1.02); heroic keeps the elite damage, +50% health, double fire rate, three times harder to suppress, self-healing, red tracers. The manual's extra heroic damage is not in the 1.02 data: uncertain entry, sources_disagree.

verdicts.claim: Cannot rank up (no ExperienceLevels): Nod and Scrin harvesters, MCVs, Surveyor, Emissary, Explorer, GDI and ZOCOM Engineers, Assimilator, Fanatics, T59 Cultists, Ox, Carryall; GDI-side harvesters rank. verdicts.reason: Confirmed.
verdicts.evidence: GDIRifleSoldierSquad 57 vs GDIRifleSoldier 62, NODMilitantSquad 43 vs NODMilitant 48 (KW XML). https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Armory: no other building or unit in TW/KW refills squads. Repair drone page: Scrin drones cannot restore members.

verdicts.claim: Suppression: never suppressed are Marked of Kane cyborgs, Fanatics and Scrin infantry ('page and manual'); the XML also gives none to Zone Troopers and Zone Raiders
verdicts.reason: The prone, quarter-speed, less-damage and cover mechanics are right, but the immunity list is wrong in three ways. (1) The manual names only Fanatics as impossible to suppress (and Grenadiers as hard); the KW manual never mentions suppression. (2) The XML gives the Fanatic a SuppressionUpdate with Suppressability 1000, the same as the Grenadier, so the page and the data disagree. (3) The XML gives no suppression to the Confessor (Militant squad leader) or the Confessor Cabal members, which the notes miss.

Kanes Wrath/Xml/NOD/Units/NODFanatic.xml SuppressionUpdate Suppressability 1000 (GDIGrenadeSoldier.xml also 1000). NODConfessor.xml and BlackHandConfessor.xml (inherits it) have no SuppressionUpdate; nor do ZT, ZR, MoK cyborgs, Scrin infantry or Cultists. GlobalData/AttributeModifier.xml Modifier_Test_Suppression ARMOR 75%, SPEED 25%.
verdicts.correction: Never suppressed (no SuppressionUpdate in the XML): Zone Troopers, Zone Raiders, the Awakened and Enlightened, all Scrin infantry including Cultists, and the Confessor and Confessor Cabal members. Fanatics: the page and their manual paragraph say never, the XML says hard but possible. Record an uncertain entry (sources_disagree).

verdicts.claim: Garrisons: up to three squads in civilian buildings, fire out with protection and extra reach, thrown out when the building is badly damaged, no repair while garrisoned; Zone Troopers, Zone Raiders and Scrin infantry other than Buzzers and Cultists cannot garrison; the listed weapons clear garrisons
verdicts.reason: This matches the Garrisoning page and the manual, and the clearer list matches the XML. But the XML garrison filter excludes only Zone Troopers, Zone Raiders, Shock Troopers, Disintegrators and Ravagers, so the Mastermind, Prodigy and Assimilator are not barred in data; that disagreement is missed.
verdicts.evidence: https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning (Tiberium Wars section). UC text, Garrisoning Infantry. BaseObjects/BaseCivilianStructure.xml HordeGarrisonContain ContainMax 3 with exactly those ExcludeThing entries. AlienAssimilator KindOf includes STEALTH_GARRISON; Mastermind and Assimilator carry SKIRMISH_AI_DONT_GARRISON (an AI flag only).
verdicts.correction: Add: the data does not bar the Mastermind, Prodigy or Assimilator from civilian garrisons (the wiki says Scrin do not garrison), so record an uncertain entry where it matters.

verdicts.claim: Transports: one squad in the APC, MRT, Hammerhead, Behemoth and Heavy Harvester; the Reckoner holds two, three once deployed; riders fire out of the APC, the Hammerhead and the deployed Reckoner, and 'check the others'
verdicts.reason: The capacities are right, but the passenger-firing set is incomplete: all five one-squad carriers let riders fire.
verdicts.evidence: XML HordeTransportContain: APC, Hammerhead, MRT, Heavy Harvester and Behemoth each have 1 slot with contained status CAN_ATTACK. NODBunkerTruck.xml has 2 slots plus 1 after Upgrade_DeployNODBunkerTruck, CAN_ATTACK only after the deploy upgrade. Wiki infoboxes of the Behemoth, Heavy harvester and Mobile Repair Transport say the garrisoned squad can attack.
verdicts.correction: Riders fire out of the APC, MRT, Hammerhead, Behemoth and Heavy Harvester, and out of the Reckoner only once deployed: passenger-sets-weapon for all six.

verdicts.claim: Riders die with the vehicle, except in the Reckoner (XML KillPassengersOnDeath)
verdicts.reason: The sources disagree, and the notes give only the XML side. The Reckoner is one object in both forms with KillPassengersOnDeath=false. The wiki says the first time its truck form is destroyed it turns into the bunker, and if the bunker is destroyed its occupants die.
verdicts.evidence: Kanes Wrath/Xml/NOD/Units/NODBunkerTruck.xml: HordeTransportContain KillPassengersOnDeath=false, deploy by upgrade on the same object. https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Reckoner_(Kane%27s_Wrath) game-unit section.
verdicts.correction: Riders die with the APC, MRT, Hammerhead, Behemoth and Heavy Harvester. The Reckoner turns into its bunker when first destroyed. Whether riders survive the bunker's destruction is disputed (XML says they survive, wiki says they die): uncertain entry.

verdicts.claim: Epic units take infantry permanently, each squad adding a hardpoint: MARV four, Redeemer two, Eradicator three
verdicts.reason: Confirmed.
verdicts.evidence: XML contain modules (MARV ContainMax 4, Redeemer 2, Eradicator 3). Garrisoning page (no exit). KW manual MARV and Eradicator paragraphs.

verdicts.claim: Call for transport: GDI (all three), Nod and Marked of Kane infantry and light and medium vehicles; not Black Hand, Scrin, heavy units, harvesters, MCVs or aircraft; for a fee and on a long recharge
verdicts.reason: The fee and recharge are confirmed (200 credits, 120 s), but two exceptions are missed. (1) The Shadow Team (Nod and MoK) has no Call for transport button in the XML and is absent from the wiki's list, although the 2007 manual lists the ability for it. (2) The KW manual lists Call for transport for the Heavy Harvester, but its command set lacks it.

SpecialPowerTemplates.xml SpecialPowerCallForTransportGDI/NOD: ReloadTime 120s, Money -200. https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Call_for_transport (lists Surveyor and Emissary, not the Shadow Team). UC text Shadow Team abilities. KW manual p.16 Heavy Harvester abilities.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Detail: the Battle Base has three drones and the MRT one.

Weapon.xml AutoReloadsClip=RETURN_TO_BASE only for GDIOrcaRocketWeapon, GDIFirehawk missile and bomb loads, NODVertigoBomb and OrcaEchoCannon (ZOCOM Orca). KW manual p.13-14 (Hammerhead; Combat Support Airfield, Nod version not for Black Hand). TW manual PDF 18 and Intel DB: an Airfield keeps up to four aircraft.

verdicts.claim: Husks: the Juggernaut, Behemoth, Avatar, Purifier, Annihilator and Reaper Tripod leave husks that any side's engineer-type unit can recover; they decay, and heavy or epic units can crush them (cited partly to manual PDF page 10); the Titan, Gun Walker, Redeemer and Eradicator leave none
verdicts.reason: The mechanic is confirmed, but the manual citation is wrong. The 2007 manual's page 10 (Beware of Engineers box) has no husk line; only the unreleased UC reprint adds one.
verdicts.evidence: https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Husk. The engineer, Combat engineer, Saboteur and Assimilator pages (capture walker husks). XML husk OCLs. TW manual page images PDF 10, 16 and 24.
verdicts.correction: Cite the Engineer paragraph (PDF 16) and the Assimilator paragraph (PDF 24) of the 2007 manual, not PDF 10.

verdicts.claim: Crushing: the listed non-crushers; heavy crushers also run over heavy infantry and light vehicles; the MARV, Eradicator and Redeemer crush every non-epic unit; heavy infantry escape ordinary vehicles; Commandos, Mastermind, Prodigy and Buzzers are crushable only by epic units
verdicts.reason: The levels are right, but: (1) heavy crushers (level 3) run over every ordinary vehicle (crushable 2), the Predator and Scorpion included, not only light ones; (2) the Mechapede (0/2) is missing from the non-crushers; (3) Dozer Blades raise the Scorpion's and Reckoner's crusher level to 2, so upgraded they crush heavy infantry; (4) the Titan slows down while crushing vehicles, and since KW 1.01 Titans cannot crush Titans.
verdicts.evidence: XML CrusherInfo: BaseVehicle 1/2; Mammoth, Juggernaut, Behemoth, Titan, Avatar, Purifier and both Tripods 3/3; epic units 4/4; AlienCustomizableVehicle 0/2.
