Official role labels in the Intelligence Database that count at roles.secondary step 1, all missed (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Intelligence_Database): the Venom is called a VTOL scout (InOps Nod Aircraft); the Zone Raider's role became a first-response scouting unit; the Beam Cannon is called an artillery system and Nod's long-range artillery platform (Beam Cannon and Obelisk entries); the Flame Tank is a classic anti-infantry weapon system and flamethrowers are anti-infantry weapons (Flame Weapons entry); the Slingshot is an exclusively anti-air vehicle; the Hammerhead is an assault/transport hybrid; the Vertigo is a stealth bomber; the Sniper Team carries a spotter. In the 2007 manual's Mortars upgrade text (PDF 19), the Pitbull's main jobs are scouting and shooting at aircraft.

Official strong-against text missed (matters for step 4 and the drop rule): the Stealth Tank's DB entry (missiles good against vehicles and structures) contradicts the notes' 'no official strength'; the Avatar's DB entry (its laser does great harm to vehicles and buildings); the Sniper Team (kills most infantry); the Black Hand (incinerates enemy squads); Buzzers (flesh and light armour); Disintegrators (vehicles); Shock Troopers (armoured vehicles head-on); the Corrupter (humans); the Combat Engineer (enemy Engineers). Sources: UC/TW manual paragraphs, KW manual p.16, Intel DB.

XML-versus-wiki/manual disagreements beyond the Scorpion, each needing an uncertain entry: Stormrider shroud (wiki 500, XML 400); Ravager sight (wiki gives the member's 300/320, the squad object has 350/400); Reckoner riders on death; Heavy Harvester Call for transport (KW manual yes, XML no); Shadow Team Call for transport (2007 manual yes, KW XML and wiki no); Fanatic suppression (page and manual never, XML Suppressability 1000); Scrin garrisons (BaseCivilianStructure.xml bars only Shock Trooper, Disintegrator and Ravager squads, so the Mastermind, Prodigy and Assimilator are not barred); heroic damage (manual more, AttributeModifier.xml equal to elite); Tiberium Core Missiles (KW manual lists SAM, Stealth Tank and Mantis, but the wiki and XML also give the Attack Bike an upgraded missile).

EA's CnC_Modding_Support repository also holds unreleased branches proposed_kw_1.03 (af82415, 2025-05-08, 117 files changed) and proposed_tw_1.10 (2d0be8c). The notes should say to read main (Kane's Wrath 1.02, TheVersion 114) only, since github.com folder views can land on another branch.

Suppression details missed: the XML gives no suppression to the Confessor (Militant squad leader) or the Confessor Cabal members (NODConfessor.xml and BlackHandConfessor.xml have no SuppressionUpdate). The heroic rank makes infantry three times harder to suppress (Unit_Heroic SUPPRESSABILITY 300). A separate modifier, Modifier_Test_Suppression_ForceMove (ARMOR 125%), seems to make suppressed infantry that are force-moved take more damage; its meaning is not documented on any page.

Crush upgrades and limits missed: Dozer Blades raise the Scorpion's and Reckoner's crusher level from 1 to 2, so they then crush heavy infantry (wiki infoboxes). The Titan slows while crushing vehicles (Titan page), and since KW 1.01 Titans cannot crush Titans (KW patch 1.01 page). Heavy crushers run over every ordinary vehicle, not just light ones (Mammoth tank and Titan pages: most tier 1 and 2 vehicles). The Mechapede (AlienCustomizableVehicle, crusher 0) is not a crusher.

Armour facing on walkers: AlienGunWalkerArmor (Gun Walker, Shard Walker), AlienAnnihilatorTripodArmor (Annihilator and Reaper Tripod) and BlackHandStealthTankArmor (Mantis) all have side 110 / rear 150 in GlobalData/Armor.xml, though the notes call the walkers and Tripods directionless.

Squad-versus-member sight is not ruled on: the sight band text should say to read the squad object (for example AlienStalkerSquad 350/400), because the wiki sometimes gives the member's figure (AlienStalker 300/320). Thirty infantry objects, the reference Rifleman squad among them, also carry height-based vision bonus keys (MaxVisionBonusPercent 300, VisionBonusTestRadius 200, VisionBonusPercentPerFoot 1) that no page documents; mention them as unverified rather than banding on them.
Fog of war exception missed: superweapons can be aimed into fog (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Fog_of_war).

Speed band consequence missed: the Ravager squad moves 75 (1.32 times 57, medium), so raider's requires fail despite its hit-and-run paragraph. Use the infantry squad figure, not the KW manual's 'fastest infantry' line.

candidates.name: Sniper Team
candidates.role_guess: marksman; secondary scout (hidden while still, detects stealth)
candidates.teaches: Camouflage that depends on standing still, plus a spotter link. The two-man team (sniper and spotter) cannot be seen while it does not move, holds its fire by default until enemies detect it, outranges riflemen by far and sees cloaked units. Anything in its sight can be hit by the Juggernaut's long-range Bombard, so one cheap scout becomes the eyes of a teammate's artillery walker. Since KW 1.02, spotting for a Bombard no longer reveals it.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for GDI and ZOCOM (Steel Talons lack it). Gate: Armory (t2). Cost $1000 (medium band). A minor extra, Call for Transport ($200), needs an Airfield.
candidates.shooter_note: Stand still to vanish and pick your moment for very long shots. Whatever you can see, a teammate in an artillery walker can shell, so two players make a spotter-and-gun pair.
candidates.repeats: No unit in data/units links cloak yet, and none plays a passive spotter. The spotting is passive, so it belongs in sensors, combos and the spotter team-play hook rather than a pattern. It shares cloak with the Shadow Team, which teaches the glider instead.

candidates.name: Rig
candidates.role_guess: support (infobox: support vehicle); secondary area-denial once deployed
candidates.teaches: A deployable forward base. While driving, the Rig is unarmed and fragile. On flat open ground it unfolds into a Battle Base with twin cannons, an anti-air launcher, three drones that repair nearby vehicles, stealth detection and self-repair, and it can pack up again (KW 1.01 sped up both). The lesson is a support player who becomes the team's frontline repair station.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for GDI, Steel Talons and ZOCOM. Gate: Command Post (t2). Cost $2000 (high band). In KW, GDI and Steel Talons get a railgun upgrade for the Battle Base.
candidates.shooter_note: Drive a defenceless truck to a chokepoint, unfold it into a fortified post whose drones mend teammates' vehicles, and pack up when the front moves. A strong anchor that needs an escort while it moves.
candidates.repeats: In data/units, deploy-siege-mode is linked by the RA2 Desolator, Siege Chopper and Slave Miner. The twist here is that the deployed form is a small base with repair drones and both ground and air guns.

candidates.name: Orca
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (infobox: ground attack aircraft); secondary scout
candidates.teaches: Detection you can stick onto things. Pulse Scan reveals stealth around the Orca on a key (1 min cooldown). Sensor Pods (a Command Post upgrade, $100 each) can be fired onto the ground, a structure or an enemy vehicle and reveal hidden units around them for two minutes, so a pod on an enemy tank keeps exposing cloaked units around it as it drives. The Orca also carries few rockets (6, or 9 with KW Hardpoints) and must rearm at its pad.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for GDI and Steel Talons. Gate: Airfield (t2). Cost $1100 (medium band). The pages disagree on the Sensor Pod cooldown: the Sensor pods page gives 60 s, the Orca page gives none.
candidates.shooter_note: A strike VTOL with a few heavy rockets that must fly home to rearm. It tags enemy vehicles or ground with sensors that keep hidden enemies visible to the whole team.
candidates.repeats: In data/units, reveal-area is linked only by the RA1 Spy's one-shot Sonar Pulse. The twist here is a sensor that rides on a moving enemy. Rearming at a pad echoes the RA1 Yak.

candidates.name: Zone Shatterer
candidates.role_guess: anti-infantry (a guess: the infobox says support vehicle, but it has no support parts)
candidates.teaches: A power shot paid for with a self-stun. Overload Beam fires a stronger sonic blast with a little more reach, then leaves the hovertank disabled and unable to move for about 6 seconds. Its normal weapon is a forward-fixed sonic emitter that hits every unit along its line and fires through or over buildings, so the hull has to turn to aim and cannot shoot on the move.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in Kane's Wrath skirmish and multiplayer, ZOCOM only. GDI and Steel Talons build the plain Shatterer ($1500), which lacks Overload. Gate: Command Post (t2). Cost $1600 (high band; KW 1.01 price). It would probably be coded variant_of cnc3.gdi.shatterer.
candidates.shooter_note: A drifting hovertank whose forward-fixed sonic cannon pierces lines of enemies and walls. The Overload key trades six helpless seconds for one big blast.
candidates.repeats: No unit in data/units links fire-power-shot. The class is hover because of its HoverTech drive, but whether it can cross water is unchecked; if it cannot, class it as a vehicle.

candidates.name: Saboteur
candidates.teaches: Trapping what the enemy wants to use. The unarmed Saboteur captures buildings and revives walker husks (the registry's example for recover-wreck). Its Booby Trap ($100, 20 s cooldown) rigs neutral buildings, husks, tech structures and bridges to explode when an enemy garrisons, captures or uses them, killing the engineer who tries.

new_mechanics.summary: Rig a building, wreck, bridge or capture point so it explodes on the first enemy who enters, captures or uses it.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Nod; the Black Hand subfaction builds it too, as does the Marked of Kane (MoK cybernetic legs double its speed). Gate: Hand of Nod (t1). Cost $500 (very-low band).
candidates.shooter_note: An unarmed objective player who steals buildings and revives dead walkers for the team, and booby-traps points and wrecks so the enemy's own engineer sets them off.
candidates.repeats: In data/units, the RA1 Spy links capture-structure. recover-wreck and the booby trap are new there. Boundary: lay-mines plants a mine on open ground, while the trap sits on an object the enemy will use.

candidates.name: Shadow Team
candidates.teaches: Infantry with a flight mode. On a key the squad opens gliders, travels as low fliers and lands again (since KW 1.01, airborne teams cannot force-fire at the ground). It is hidden while not attacking and plants explosive charges on structures (30 s cooldown). In KW it can also drop an Artillery Beacon: for two minutes, Specters can shell anything inside its radius.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Nod, and for its Marked of Kane subfaction. Gate: Secret Shrine (t2 in the tier map; the infobox says tier 3). Cost $800 (low band). The Artillery Beacon is Kane's Wrath only and needs Specters.
candidates.shooter_note: A cloaked commando who switches to a glider to sail over walls into the enemy rear, plants charges, and drops a beacon that a teammate's artillery can fire on.
candidates.repeats: In data/units, transform is linked by the RA3 Mecha Tengu, throw-explosive by RA3 Tanya, and bombard-area by the RA1 Spy and RA2 Boris. The twist here is personal gliding wings as the second form (mobility jetpack / wings), and a bombardment that a teammate fires.

candidates.name: Beam Cannon
candidates.role_guess: siege (infobox: light artillery vehicle; long-range direct laser)
candidates.teaches: Beams that team up. When several Beam Cannons hit one target, their beams merge and the damage grows with the square of their number. Reflector Beam (Nod and MoK only) bounces the beam off a stationary Venom nearby to reach distant targets, aircraft included. Charge Defenses lets up to four of them raise an Obelisk of Light's fire rate, sight and range.

new_mechanics.summary: Beams from several units of one type on the same target fuse into one beam whose damage grows faster than their number.
Bounce your shot off a stationary friendly unit to reach targets beyond your own range, including fliers your weapon could not otherwise hit.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Nod; the Black Hand subfaction builds it too, as does the Marked of Kane. Gate: Operations Center (t2). Cost $1000 (medium band). Only Nod and MoK get Reflector Beam, since Black Hand has no Venom.
candidates.shooter_note: A fragile long-range laser vehicle that wants company: several players' stacked beams melt one target, a hovering teammate becomes a mirror for anti-air shots, and it can overcharge a friendly turret.
candidates.repeats: No unit in data/units links rally-allies, and none merges or relays beams. merge-beams fits the swarm team-play hook, so the trim could keep it as a hook or a weapon trait rather than a new pattern.

candidates.name: Avatar
candidates.teaches: A walker that grows by absorbing other units. Commandeer Technology destroys a chosen Nod unit to add a fixed part: a Beam Cannon gives a second laser, a Flame Tank a flamethrower that clears garrisons, an Attack Bike stealth detection, and a Stealth Tank stealth while not firing. It also works on enemy Nod vehicles, and for a few seconds on the wreck of a targeted vehicle. Its lasers fire only while it stands still, and it leaves a husk that any side's engineers can revive.

new_mechanics.summary: Consume a friendly unit or its fresh wreck to permanently gain a part tied to that unit type, such as its weapon, stealth or detector.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Nod, and for its Marked of Kane subfaction (Black Hand gets the Purifier instead). Gate: Tech Lab (t3). Cost $2200 (very-high band). The wiki has no Commandeer Technology page, so cite the unit page.
candidates.shooter_note: A big walker that builds its own loadout by eating wrecks or willing allies (flamer, stealth, detector, second laser), and has to plant its feet to fire.
candidates.repeats: In data/units, leech-weapon-on-kill is the RA3 Hammer Tank's. The twist here is friendly donors, one fixed part per donor type, and parts that are abilities (stealth, detection) as well as weapons.

candidates.name: Purifier
candidates.role_guess: assault (infobox: heavy assault walker); secondary buffer
candidates.teaches: A walking morale aura. Friendly infantry squads near the Purifier fire 50% faster, gain 25% armour and are harder to suppress. Garrisoned troops do not get the boost, and several Purifiers do not stack. It is the Avatar chassis with a built-in flamethrower that clears garrisons, but it cannot commandeer, has no anti-air and leaves a revivable husk.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in Kane's Wrath skirmish and multiplayer, Black Hand only. Gate: Tech Lab (t3). Cost $3000 (very-high band). Its Purifying Flame upgrade comes from the Black Hand Secret Shrine.
candidates.shooter_note: A slow flame-and-laser walker that acts as the infantry's banner: foot soldiers near it shoot faster and shrug off hits. It leads pushes but needs an anti-air escort.
candidates.repeats: It shares the Avatar's chassis and could be coded variant_of cnc3.nod.avatar, so keep only one of the two if the trim needs room. No unit in data/units links rally-allies yet, and this aura is its cleanest example on the list.

candidates.name: Buzzers
candidates.teaches: Riding on a teammate. Combine with Vehicle attaches the swarm to a friendly Scrin ground vehicle, where it cannot be harmed and attacks nearby infantry on its own until ordered off or the host dies. On its own it is a cheap, fragile swarm of airborne blades that only hurts infantry, clears garrisons, can shelter in buildings but not fire from them, and heals in Tiberium.

new_mechanics.summary: Latch onto a friendly vehicle, immune while riding it, and keep fighting from it until you let go or the host dies.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Scrin, Reaper-17 and Traveler-59. Gate: Portal (t1). Cost $200 (very-low band). Buzzers released by Buzzer Hive defences cannot be controlled.
candidates.shooter_note: A tiny, cheap swarm player that shreds soldiers and clears buildings, and can latch onto a teammate's vehicle to ride along untouchable as its anti-infantry guard.
candidates.repeats: The RA3 Terror Drone (infest-vehicle) latches onto enemies; Buzzers latch onto allies. Boundary: passenger-sets-weapon's fire-ports variant covers riders who fire from inside a vehicle, while Buzzers ride outside and keep their own attack. The wiki calls them the Scrin basic infantry; drone follows our rule for small uncrewed units.

candidates.name: Ravager
candidates.role_guess: assault (infobox: assault infantry); secondary anti-armour (its shards do bonus damage to vehicles)
candidates.teaches: A counter keyed to the target's cargo. Tiberium Agitation (45 s cooldown) hurts anything holding Tiberium, more the more it carries (up to double) and half on empty ones. That punishes harvesters, refineries, silos and Tiberium-fed units, Scrin ones included. The three-alien squad fires shards, resists gunfire and heals in Tiberium.

new_mechanics.summary: On a key, set off the resource an enemy is carrying, so the hit grows with how full it is.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in Kane's Wrath skirmish and multiplayer for all three Scrin factions (upgrades: Blue Shards for R17, Advanced Articulators for T59). Gates: Stasis Chamber and Nerve Center (t2). Cost $1200 (medium band).
candidates.shooter_note: A tough shard-gun trooper whose blast reads the enemy's load: harvesters, loot carriers and resource-powered vehicles take extra, so it hunts the economy.
candidates.repeats: Nothing in data/units scales damage with what the target carries. deal-percent-damage (RA1 MAD Tank) scales with the target's health, not its cargo.

candidates.name: Devourer Tank
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (a guess; infobox: medium tank; weak against infantry, no anti-air)
candidates.teaches: Ammunition drawn from the economy. Conversion Beam drains a nearby Tiberium field or an allied Extractor or Refinery to fill a store of supercharged shots: $100 of Tiberium fills it and each shot spends $10, so 10 shots (20 with the Reaper-17 Conversion Reserves upgrade). Its hull moves in any direction like a turret, it outranges every other non-artillery unit, and Buzzers can ride on it.

new_mechanics.summary: Draw from a resource node or a friendly refinery to load a limited stock of stronger shots, each shot spending some of it.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Scrin and Reaper-17 (Traveler-59 lacks it). Gate: Nerve Center (t2). Cost $1600 (high band). KW 1.02 cut its range.
candidates.shooter_note: A strafing energy tank that refills supercharged shots at a resource node or friendly refinery, so it fights near the economy and outranges other tanks.
candidates.repeats: gather-resources (RA2 Slave Miner) banks resources, while this unit spends them as ammo. The Reaper-17 Reaper tripod has the same Conversion Beam.

candidates.name: Mechapede
candidates.role_guess: assault (a guess; infobox: customizable support walker)
candidates.teaches: A body built segment by segment in the field. The head can buy up to 8 segments, each taking about a second, of four kinds: shards against infantry and vehicles; a Tiberium spray that hurts infantry and heals Scrin units, itself included; a disintegrator against armour; and discs, its only anti-air. Each segment has its own health. Losing one drops every segment behind it, and killing the head kills them all. It is very fast, cannot reverse, fires in any direction and sees stealth.

new_mechanics.summary: Add body segments mid-life, each with its own weapon and health; losing one also loses every segment behind it.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, in Kane's Wrath skirmish and multiplayer for Scrin, Reaper-17 and Traveler-59. Gate: Technology Assembler (t3). Cost $1400 for the head (medium band) plus $100 per segment.
candidates.shooter_note: A snake-like walker whose loadout is its length. Buy segments mid-fight to mix anti-infantry, anti-armour, anti-air and healing, and guard the tail, because each lost segment cuts off the rest.
candidates.repeats: No unit in data/units links upgrade-in-field yet, and the segment chain is new. Its healing spray is the Corrupter's weapon, so the Corrupter is left off the list.

candidates.name: Planetary Assault Carrier
candidates.role_guess: assault (a guess; infobox: heavy capital ship)
candidates.teaches: A carrier with no gun of its own: its swarm is the weapon, and it can call up a weather zone. Up to 8 Invader fighters hit air and ground, are replaced for free over time and die with the carrier (weapon family drone-launcher, not the launch-drones pattern, which covers only the version on a key). Ion Storm works only while the carrier is parked, ends if it moves and has a 1 min cooldown: the local storm makes Scrin aircraft deal more damage, take less and heal, while lightning strikes nearby enemies. Forcefield Generators add a recharging shield.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, in skirmish and multiplayer for Scrin and Traveler-59 (Reaper-17 lacks it). Gate: Signal Transmitter (t3 in the tier map; the wiki says tier 4). Cost $3000 (very-high band). Forcefield Generators are Scrin only; Traveler-59's Traveler Engines make it faster.
candidates.shooter_note: A slow flying mothership: your fighters do the shooting and come back on their own, and parking calls a storm that buffs and heals friendly fliers and zaps nearby enemies.
candidates.repeats: In data/units, leave-hazard-zone is linked by the RA2 Desolator. The twist here is one zone that is home ground for allies and a hazard for enemies, raised only while parked. The Invader swarm belongs with the drone-launcher family (the RA2 Aircraft Carrier, not yet researched).

candidates.coverage_note:
This is 14 candidates for a batch that keeps about 9. By faction: GDI 4 (Sniper Team, Rig, Orca, ZOCOM Zone Shatterer), Nod 5 (Saboteur, Shadow Team, Beam Cannon, Avatar, Black Hand Purifier), Scrin 5 (Buzzers, Ravager, Devourer Tank, Mechapede, Planetary Assault Carrier). Four are Kane's Wrath units (Zone Shatterer and Purifier are subfaction-only; Ravager and Mechapede are new to KW), and Kane's Wrath abilities appear on the Shadow Team, Orca and Beam Cannon.

Spread:
- Classes: infantry 4, vehicle 3, walker 3, aircraft 2, hover 1, drone 1. Tiberium Wars has no ships.
- Price bands: very-low 2, low 1, medium 5, high 3, very-high 3.
- Tiers: t1 2, t2 8, t3 4.
- Roles: marksman, support, anti-armour, anti-infantry, engineer, infiltrator, siege and assault, plus buffer as a secondary.

Mechanics: the list links five registry ids that no unit in data/units has yet (cloak, fire-power-shot, recover-wreck, rally-allies, upgrade-in-field). It proposes eight new ids: booby-trap-object, merge-beams, relay-off-ally, absorb-ally-part, attach-to-ally, detonate-cargo, charge-from-resource and grow-segments. It also covers the team-play hooks spotter (Sniper, Orca, Shadow), swarm (Beam Cannon) and protector (Rig, Purifier, Buzzers).

Overlaps to weigh in the trim:
- Avatar and Purifier share a chassis.
- Sniper Team and Shadow Team both cloak; the Sniper teaches spotting, the Shadow the glider.
- rally-allies appears three times; the Purifier's aura is the cleanest example.

Left out on purpose:
- Steel Talons Titan: Adaptive Armor is a textbook case of brace, an id no researched unit has. It is the best swap if the trim wants a Steel Talons-only unit.
- Reaper-17 Reaper tripod: the same Conversion Beam as the Devourer, plus a passive EMP on its target.
- Traveler-59 Prodigy and Cultists: their teleport and mind control repeat the Chrono Legionnaire and Mastermind.
- Marked of Kane Awakened and Enlightened: their EMP is disable-machine, already taught by the Terror Drone. The Tiberium trooper's slowing spray is minor.
- MARV and Eradicator hexapod: one-per-player epics. The MARV harvests by driving over Tiberium; the hexapod's aura refunds part of the cost of enemies killed near it, which fits the share-spoils hook.
- Redeemer: its Rage Generator is confuse-enemies, already taught by the Chaos Drone.
- Vertigo: its cloaking pods are an area variant of cloak.
- Venom: its Signature Generator shows fake units on radar, a good alternate for spawn-decoy or jam-sensors.
- Stealth tank: plain cloak.
- Reckoner: a one-way bunker that also becomes one the first time it is destroyed.
- Rifleman squad: its Dig In foxhole is build-cover.
- Firehawk: loadout swapped only on the pad, and a Stratofighter boost that flies it anywhere on the map.
- Juggernaut and Specter: the artillery halves of the spotter pairs.
- Corrupter: its spray is on the Mechapede.
- Mantis, Zone raider, Behemoth, Mobile Repair Transport and Wolverine repeat other units. Shard walker and Shielded harvester only add Reaper-17's regenerating forcefields, which is an armour model, not a pattern.

Page notes:
- Each main page resolved with one API request. MARV redirects to Mammoth Armored Reclamation Vehicle and Walker husk to Husk; there are no pages for Commandeer Technology or Glider pack.
- The Sensor Pod cooldown differs between the Orca and Sensor pods pages.
- The infoboxes put the Shadow Team at tier 3 and the carrier at tier 4, against t2 and t3 in the tier map.
- Prices are the Kane's Wrath infobox values. The sibling notes-cnc3 run found EA's CnC_Modding_Support XML with KW 1.02 values, which can settle doubts; that run also has the Scorpion at 800, not the 700 in the cost-anchor note.
- Apostrophes in URLs are written %27, as in data/units.
